messages:
marta: Heads-up — proposing an "ephemeral lock" pattern for config changes that require manual approval. Idea: when someone starts a rollout from the console or API, we create a short-lived lock (TTL 10m) that prevents concurrent rollouts and surfaces an approval queue. Keeps config collisions low and makes rollbacks deterministic.
lee: curious — how does the lock get created for API users? will it be a separate call or part of the rollout POST?
marta: plan is to make it part of the rollout POST. example:
```
POST /v1/configs/rollouts
{ "policy": "cohorted", "create_lock": true, "lock_ttl": 600 }
```
server returns 409 if there's an active lock, includes lock owner + expiry.
jordan: how will this look in the console? product wants minimal clicks for PLG users.
marta: console will show a banner with lock owner, ETA and two buttons: "request takeover" (sends notification) and "wait/monitor". approval flow stays in the SMR modal for enterprise users.
sara: rollbacks — how do we ensure a rollback can bypass the lock in emergencies? ops needs a deadman's switch.
lee: propose an "override" path allowed only for people in the ops-sudo group and requires a signed justification stored in audit logs.
sam-sre: agreed on signed justification. also we should emit a rollback-signal event to the routing service so caches invalidate and canary traffic is immediately drained.
ops-bot: AUTOMATION: preflight checks ran (config lint, quota sanity, telemetry sampling) — all green :white_check_mark:
marta: telemetry gating: we should require a minimum telemetry sampling window (e.g., 5m) after canary to avoid false negatives. the lock TTL can be auto-extended while gating metrics are still ambiguous.
jordan: don't want locks to hang forever — what's the auto-extend policy?
marta: max 3 extensions, each up to 5m, and a manual snooze with audit entry. after that, expiration and automatic rollback to previous stable if no action.
sara: how do we audit intent? need a link in the audit entry to the prompt/eval set used for the rollout so later quality regressions are traceable.
lee: question for API design: should the lock be a resource with its own ID? that would let clients poll or watch via websocket.
marta: yes. expose /v1/locks/{id} with status, owner, history. also push via websocket for console live updates.
sam-sre: small note — make sure lock creation is idempotent for retries (client-supplied idempotency-key) to avoid duplicate locks from flaky devices.
jordan: UX concern — PLG users might be surprised by 409. add inline guidance in the console and a "request takeover" flow sending an ephemeral DM to the owner.
marta: agreed. I'll draft an API spec and console mocks. aim to land RFC by EOD Friday. tagging @sam-sre for failure-mode review, @lee for API surface, and @jordan for console copy.
sam-sre: I'll simulate the emergency override path and test event emission for routing invalidation tomorrow.
lee: I'll sketch the /locks API and idempotency semantics today.
jordan: will do the console copy + modal mockups.
marta: rough TODOs: RFC, API impl, console banner + takeover flow, websocket push, telemetry gating logic, audit link to evals. thanks all :sparkles:
